input: Research accessible hiking trails for wheelchair users

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The geographic area (local, regional, national, or a specific destination) completely determines which trails to research — a local search vs. a national parks overview are entirely different tasks.
Knowing who the wheelchair user is (e.g., manual vs. power chair, adult vs. child, solo vs. group) affects which accessibility standards and trail features matter most.
Whether this is for a specific upcoming trip or general future reference changes the urgency and depth of research needed.
Physical constraints like maximum trail length, elevation gain tolerance, or surface type (paved, packed gravel, boardwalk) narrow the list dramatically.
Scenic priorities (forests, mountains, water, wildlife) or amenities (restrooms, parking, picnic areas) shape which trails are worth highlighting.
Knowing the desired output — a shortlist of trails, a detailed guide, a comparison table — determines how thorough and structured the research needs to be.
Whether the user wants to do the research themselves with a plan, or needs a ready-made compiled resource, determines the immediate next action and tools to use.

gold.taskDescription: Find and compile information about hiking trails that are accessible for wheelchair users.

questions.title: What geographic area or region should be covered?
questions.description: Determine whether the research should focus on a specific city, state, national park, country, or a destination the user already has in mind.

questions.title: Who is the wheelchair user — manual or power chair?
questions.description: Identify the type of wheelchair and the user's mobility profile, as this directly affects which trail surfaces and grades are suitable.

questions.title: Is this for a specific upcoming trip or future planning?
questions.description: Clarify whether there is a fixed travel date driving urgency, or if this is exploratory research for a trip not yet scheduled.

questions.title: What is the maximum comfortable trail length or duration?
questions.description: Establish a distance or time limit for trails to ensure recommendations match the user's physical stamina and practical needs.

questions.title: What kind of scenery or natural setting is most appealing?
questions.description: Find out whether the user prefers coastal, forested, lakeside, desert, or mountain settings to prioritize the most enjoyable options.

questions.title: What should the final output of this research look like?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants a shortlist, a detailed write-up per trail, a comparison table, or a saved reference document.

questions.title: Which tools or sources should be used for the research?
questions.description: Establish whether to use specific websites (AllTrails, NPS, local parks authority), apps, or community forums, and whether the user will conduct the research or needs it compiled for them.
